# Simployer One - Recruitment - Getting started

Getting started

Five easy steps to get ready to post your first job. (Sections with * are likely to differ from partner to partner, so please ensure they represent your process)

Just getting started on Recruitment? Complete these five simple steps to get ready to post your first job:

1. Create your Privacy Policy

Candidates are required to accept your privacy policy when they apply to one of your roles to ensure compliance with GDPR.

To generate a policy for your company, go to Settings - Data & Privacy - Privacy Policy .

For more details on creating your privacy policy, please review our guide.

2. Add team members and manage their permission levels*

Managing access to Recruitment is possible from within the HRIS core platform. <Customise as required from HRIS .>

For more details on managing team member access, take a look at our guide on managing users. You can also find a breakdown of permission levels.

3. Set Up Integrations

Our calendar integration, Cronofy, allows you to automate interview scheduling through Recruitment . By allowing access to your calendar availability, Recruitment can offer available slots to candidates to self-schedule interviews, saving you lots of valuable time. You can set this up under Settings - Integrations - My Integrations - Automatic Interview Scheduling - Cronofy .

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

Note: if you are syncing with a work Microsoft calendar, you are likely to need to use Office365 to authenticate your account.

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

You can set your diary availability under Settings - Personal - My Preferences .

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

Integrating your email allows you to communicate with candidates through the platform through your own email address. We integrate with both Google and Microsoft. You can set this up under Settings - Integrations - My Integrations - Email Candidates .

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

Note: if you are using your business Microsoft account, it’s likely you need to select Office365 to complete your authentication after selecting “Connect” on the Microsoft button.

4. Set Up Your Career site

Simployer Recruitment enables you to set up a Career Page quickly and easily, helping you promote your Employer Value Proposition and greatly increase candidate interest in working for your business.

If you are creating your career page for the first time in Simployer Recruitment , head to Settings - Career Site - Customise to get started. Click on the Setting wheel to get started.

If you are looking to integrate your existing career page with Recruitment , you can head to Settings - Career Site - Customise to find your iFrame code. Take a look at our guides here for more detail. We also enable an API integration, should you wish to expore that. This is available via Settings – Integrations – Jobs API.

Note: you may need support from an IT contact within your organisation to get this integration up and running.

5. Create your first job

You're now ready to set your first job live!

Go to the Jobs section on the navigations bar, and select Add New Job . You’ll be taken through a 6 step process to get your job live:

Job Details: job description, salary, location and job advert Job Options: screening questions, blind hiring, candidate match score, job access and notifications Interview Stages: select the number and type of interviews you’ll be having Interview Details: add your hiring team and set up any automations you wish to use (such as interview scheduling) Scorecards: select the skills, values and competencies you wish to evaluate the candidates against for this job Share: advertise your job through socials channels and job

h1: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment
Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: Simployer Recruitment`s interview scheduling allows you to automate the scheduling of interviews, offering candidates a 1-1 interview, either by phone, video or in-person, or supporting panel style interviews with multiple client-side attendees, or sequential interviews where multiple interviewers take part in a single interview stage as different times, eg ‘Hiring Manager A’ doing 30-mins followed by 45-mins with ‘Hiring Manager B’.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: The first thing to do to enable automated interview scheduling is to connect to Cronofy, our API which enables us to gather your live calendar availability.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: To set this up, head to Settings - Integrations - My Integrations .
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: Then, find Cronofy and click Connect . You will be prompted to integrate your individual work email account. You will receive a success message, and the button with show as “Disconnect” once the integration is complete.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: Note: we do not support integration with shared inboxes through Cronofy as this integration requires a personal calendar to be available to select slots from.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: Note : If your company uses Microsoft for business, the highest likelihood is that you have Microsoft 365 – please ensure you select Office 365 from the Cronofy options, not Outlook.com, for example.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

blocks.text: Once you have integrated your calendar, you can set your availability for interviews  by going to Settings – Personal – My Preferences. Here you can select your date format, time zone and the days and hours that you wish to be available for interview, in conjunction with your live calendar availability

Approvers – you are able to add an approval to the job, should that be required. You can add one or more approvers, and then select whether you want one, multiple or all approvers to approve the position. As part of the job set up process, you can decide on key skills, values and competencies that you would want your successful candidate to have. Setting this out for a role helps to avoid bias, by ensuring that all candidates are assessed against the same competencies, and potentially even add guidance notes or questions to help the interviewers and to make sure each candidate is asked the same questions during the interview.

images.context_before: You'll also see the option to specify the type of interview you wish to carry out. We offer 5 main types if interview through Recruitment : A phone call A video Q&A - ask the candidate a series of questions in text format, and they will then record their answers to on a video which will then be returned to their candidate profile on Recruitment Video – live 2-way video interview. Note: This feature is unavailable if you are using blind hiring.

Add a new job in Simployer Recruitment

The Jobs tab in Recruitment will show you all of your vacancies - live roles, archived roles, and drafts.

Head to Add New Job to start building out a new vacancy. Recruitment will guide you through a six-step process, as follows:

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

Job Details: job description, salary, location Job Options: screening questions, blind hiring, candidate match score, job access and notifications Interview Stages: outline your interview process – how many stages and what types of interview Interview Details: specifics of each stage, enabling you to add the relevant team members and set up any desired automation (such as interview scheduling) Scorecards: determine the skills, values and competencies you're looking for in this hire. These will form the basis of the scorecard that interviewers will be asked to evaluate against Share: advertise your job through socials media platforms and job boards

Job Owner/Hiring Manager/Approver - what's the difference?

Note: It’s important to know that this section will help you understand job level access to jobs and the corresponding notifications. If you want to consider and potentially alter the overall permission levels of users, please see the “Manage User Permissions” section

Under the Job Options stage of set up, you'll see these options, which determine job access and notifications:

Hiring Manager - this person will get notifications when significant changes happen, such as when a candidate is moved to the Offered or Hired stages. It’s not mandatory to have a Hiring Manager on the job, and many clients choose to not add one, as they want to minimise notifications going to the Hiring Manager unless they are very involved in the process.

Job Owner – it is mandatory to have a Job Owner and it will default to whoever is creating the job. The intention is that the Job Owner would be the main user of Recruitment for the job, meaning they would want full access and to be kept up to date with alerts relating to the position.

Approvers – you are able to add an approval to the job, should that be required. You can add one or more approvers, and then select whether you want one, multiple or all approvers to approve the position. Until the job has been approved, it will not go live, so please be mindful of that before adding an approval process!

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

What is Blind Hiring?

Note: Blind hiring can only be enabled during the creation of a new job listing and only applies to new applicants.

Blind Hiring is a feature in Recruitment which redacts key candidate information from their CV such as name, gender and ethnicit with a view to reducing the unconscious bias that these attributes could contribute towards the hiring process.

In redacting this information, it helps hiring managers to assess candidates based on their abilities alone, reducing the impact of bias and promoting a more diverse workforce.

Blind Hiring is not a default setting when creating a new role listing, but you can enable this in the second step of your role creation, Job Options, by pressing the Turn on Blind Hiring button:

Blind Hiring ends when a candidate is moved beyond the screening interview stage as personal information about the candidate is now known to the interviewer.

After the screening interview stage, their information will be permanently revealed, even if the candidate moves back to the initial stage.

Note: It's not possible to switch blind hiring on/off once you have candidates in the pipeline

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

Creating and using Scorecards

Scorecards can help you ensure fairness and clarity in your hiring process, as you work to determine who is the best fit for the job. As part of the job set up process, you can decide on key skills, values and competencies that you would want your successful candidate to have. Setting this out for a role helps to avoid bias, by ensuring that all candidates are assessed against the same competencies, and potentially even add guidance notes or questions to help the interviewers and to make sure each candidate is asked the same questions during the interview.

You can create your Scorecard for a role at the Scorecard stage of the job set up process. Scorecards can have multiple competencies, and each can also be broken down further with sub-competencies. You can either use one of our in-built competencies or free text your own.

You also have a notes section, where you can leave any guidance for your interviewers on what to look out for or to specify which questions you wish the interviewers to ask.

Creating a Scorecard template

You may find you are frequently looking for the same competencies, especially across similar seniority levels or departments. In this circumstance, it might be more effective to create a template that can then be imported as part of the job creation process.

To set up a scorecard, or to edit or delete and existing one, go to Settings - Recruitment - Scorecard Templates :

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

You can then use your Scorecard template when setting up a job at the Scorecard stage of the process. Click Import Scorecard to select which template you would like to use.

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

Note : you cannot update the Scorecard used for a job once a candidate in the process has had it filled out.

Completing a Scorecard as an interviewer

Interviewers will receive an email reminding them to complete a Scorecard shortly before the interview. The Scorecard asks them to rate the candidate from 1 to 5 on each competency and gives the opportunity to leave any notes on the candidate.

When the interviewer saves their Scorecard, their rankings will combine with any other Scorecards provided over the course of the interviews the candidate has had for that job, and will be averaged giving an overall Scorecard score. You can view their Scorecards in the Scorecards tab on the right-hand side of their profile .

It is also visible from the job kanban, next to the candidate's name:

Note: only one Scorecard can be completed per interviewer for a candidate. Interviewers can update their existing Scorecards by going into the candidate's Profile - Scorecards - Edit .

Once you have scorecards against numerous candidates in one kanban column, you can choose to compare their scorecards against eachother. To do this, select the candidates you want to compare using the select buttons on the left of their candidate card, then select Other – Compare scorecards from the bar at the bottom.

This will give you a view of all of the Scorecards left for those candidates, allowing you to get a view of where their strengths are, and see where there are notes that have been added by interviewers.

Should you wish to see more detail, you can select a specific candidate to see all of their scorecards side-by-side. Simply select either their name or the link to the notes and you will see a view similar to this:

Generate your job description with AI

Writing a job advert can be time consuming. To support businesses who don’t have a job advert prepared for their job, Recruitment has an in-built advert generator using ChatGPT to help create a basic advert that can then be customised by the client.

You can find the Description field under the Job Details part of your set up process.

When you click Generate with AI , you can select the tone of voice you like to use - friendly, fun or professional. Recruitment will then use ChatGPT to create a simple template for your required job.

[IMAGE: Screenshot]

Candidate Match Scoring

Understanding how Recruitment helps you see the best candidate matches for your role

Note: Recruitment Match Scoring is currently only available in English

How is a ‘candidate match score’ calculated?

When a candidate applies for a role, we use AI to evaluate their CV against the job description, to help you make a better decision of who to focus on.

This score is based on an algorithm that considers multiple factors, such as job title and skills as taken from the CV, which is then scored against the requirements in the job advert. You can hover over the score to see whether the candidate is a good match for job title and/or key skills in their job advert.

When setting up a job, you can determine the % match you deem a good threshold to be a match with your job. Scorecards , which are filled in by interviewers once they have interviewed a candidate, will take precedence over the candidate match score, although the candidates match score will still appear on the candidate profile underneath the candidate name, should you wish to review it at a later date.

When you sync your team member, the candidate’s information will sync into your HRIS. The exact details sent across may vary, but the standard tends to include:

Recruitment Fields to be synced

First name

Last name

Phone

Email

Job title

Start date

Adding a recruitment agency

Note: before you invite your recruitment agency partner to be a part of your Recruitment PSL of suppliers, first add the job that you would like to add them to. Once they have been created as a user, you will be able to add them as you create a job, if you prefer.

Add a new recruitment agency

To set up a new recruitment agency, navigate to Settings – Company – Agencies – Add new agency. There you can fill in information such as agency name, rate you work with them at and upload any terms that have been agreed. You also have a box to write any notes, for example the roles that you might use them for.

Once you ‘save’ you’ll have the option to add them to an existing role. Simply select the job your wish to share with the recruiter from the drop down.

Then you can add the individual recruiter from the agency that you want to add to Recruitment . To do this, type the email address of the user and press enter or select the ‘Add’ button.

Note: If you try to proceed without actually adding the user on the popup first, it will tell you that you need to first select a user.

Managing your recruitment agencies

Note: Only Account Owners and Account Admins can add and manage agencies

Manage users in an existing agency

Head to Settings - Company – Agencies . If you click on the name of the agency, you will be able to see which users have been added. It will show you which have successfully completed onboarding, which which have been invited but not yet accepted. Should you wish to resend the invite, that is possible. Please ensure the user checks their junk if they don’t receive the invite.

Clicking on the number of candidates they have submitted will bring up the profiles of these candidates, so you are able to track their effectiveness. This also tracks through to your source reporting, ensuring you get a good view as to which agencies are performing for your company.

Deactivate a recruitment agency

If you are no longer working with an agency, you can deactivate them by heading to Settings - Company - Agencies – Deactivate . Deactivating an agency will not delete it from your account, and will only "pause" the ability to send through more candidates. You can simply reactivate the agency when needed through the same page.

Upload your agreed terms

Head to Settings - Company - Agencies - Terms - Upload .

Update your existing terms

Head to Settings - Company – Agencies. Click on the three dots to the far right hand side of the row with the correct agency name and select Change Terms .

Inviting recruiters to a job

Note: Only Account Owners and Admins are able to invite recruiters to any role. Users can only invite recruiters to roles they have created.

To invite a recruiter through the job listing, once already created, head to Jobs section, click the three dots to the far right of the row with the correct agency name in it, then click Edit . You will get a popup asking you to confirm you wish to edit the job, click Edit again. Once back in the job creation journey, select Sharing from the left sub navigation and scroll to the bottom of the page where you will see an option to Invite Agency Users . You can then type out the email address or name of the recruiter, which will start to refine down your options as you type. Select from the drop down or press enter when you have finished writing the name or typing the email, then press the ‘save’ button.

When invited into a job, recruiters will receive an email to notify them, and in-app notifications on their Recruitment dashboard (for users who have already been activated on the platform).

Invite a recruiter through the Agencies page

Head to Settings - Company – Agencies. Navigate to the three dots by the agency you wish to work your job and select invite users.

From the Invite Agency Users popup, select the job you wish to add them to, and select the correct user, then Save .

What does an agency user see?

Once set up in Recruitment , your recruiters will be able to log in to their own agency portal which will show them all the jobs that have been shared with them, along with the candidates they have submitted and the stage of the process that that candidate is currently in.

Recruiters cannot see:

Any additional settings of your account Other users or recruiters on the account (except hiring managers for roles they are invited to) Any other live or archived jobs that haven’t been shared with them The client’s candidate database Any applicants to a job that were not submitted by them

Viewing jobs

When invited into a job, recruiters will receive an email to notify them, and in-app notifications on their Recruitment dashboard (dashboard notifications only apply once the user has accepted their login).

Recruiters can see the jobs they are invited to submit candidates to by navigating to the Jobs tab on the left-hand side.

Submitting a candidate for a job

Recruiters can submit candidates for a role by clicking onto the job in question and selectiong Submit candidate .

They can then provide the candidate's details, CV, and a text or video introduction.

Viewing candidate progress

Recruiters can view the progress of candidates they have submitted by selecting the job and scrolling down to the bottom where they will be able to see their candidates. The stage each candidate is at will be displayed in the Stage column.

blocks.text: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Add a new job in Simployer Recruitment
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: The Jobs tab in Recruitment will show you all of your vacancies - live roles, archived roles, and drafts.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Head to Add New Job to start building out a new vacancy. Recruitment will guide you through a six-step process, as follows:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Job Details: job description, salary, location Job Options: screening questions, blind hiring, candidate match score, job access and notifications Interview Stages: outline your interview process – how many stages and what types of interview Interview Details: specifics of each stage, enabling you to add the relevant team members and set up any desired automation (such as interview scheduling) Scorecards: determine the skills, values and competencies you're looking for in this hire. These will form the basis of the scorecard that interviewers will be asked to evaluate against Share: advertise your job through socials media platforms and job boards
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Job Owner/Hiring Manager/Approver - what's the difference?
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: It’s important to know that this section will help you understand job level access to jobs and the corresponding notifications. If you want to consider and potentially alter the overall permission levels of users, please see the “Manage User Permissions” section
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Under the Job Options stage of set up, you'll see these options, which determine job access and notifications:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Hiring Manager - this person will get notifications when significant changes happen, such as when a candidate is moved to the Offered or Hired stages. It’s not mandatory to have a Hiring Manager on the job, and many clients choose to not add one, as they want to minimise notifications going to the Hiring Manager unless they are very involved in the process.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Job Owner – it is mandatory to have a Job Owner and it will default to whoever is creating the job. The intention is that the Job Owner would be the main user of Recruitment for the job, meaning they would want full access and to be kept up to date with alerts relating to the position.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Approvers – you are able to add an approval to the job, should that be required. You can add one or more approvers, and then select whether you want one, multiple or all approvers to approve the position. Until the job has been approved, it will not go live, so please be mindful of that before adding an approval process!
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: What is Blind Hiring?
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: Blind hiring can only be enabled during the creation of a new job listing and only applies to new applicants.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Blind Hiring is a feature in Recruitment which redacts key candidate information from their CV such as name, gender and ethnicit with a view to reducing the unconscious bias that these attributes could contribute towards the hiring process.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: In redacting this information, it helps hiring managers to assess candidates based on their abilities alone, reducing the impact of bias and promoting a more diverse workforce.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Blind Hiring is not a default setting when creating a new role listing, but you can enable this in the second step of your role creation, Job Options, by pressing the Turn on Blind Hiring button:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Blind Hiring ends when a candidate is moved beyond the screening interview stage as personal information about the candidate is now known to the interviewer.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: After the screening interview stage, their information will be permanently revealed, even if the candidate moves back to the initial stage.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: It's not possible to switch blind hiring on/off once you have candidates in the pipeline
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Creating and using Scorecards
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Scorecards can help you ensure fairness and clarity in your hiring process, as you work to determine who is the best fit for the job. As part of the job set up process, you can decide on key skills, values and competencies that you would want your successful candidate to have. Setting this out for a role helps to avoid bias, by ensuring that all candidates are assessed against the same competencies, and potentially even add guidance notes or questions to help the interviewers and to make sure each candidate is asked the same questions during the interview.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You can create your Scorecard for a role at the Scorecard stage of the job set up process. Scorecards can have multiple competencies, and each can also be broken down further with sub-competencies. You can either use one of our in-built competencies or free text your own.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You also have a notes section, where you can leave any guidance for your interviewers on what to look out for or to specify which questions you wish the interviewers to ask.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Creating a Scorecard template
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You may find you are frequently looking for the same competencies, especially across similar seniority levels or departments. In this circumstance, it might be more effective to create a template that can then be imported as part of the job creation process.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: To set up a scorecard, or to edit or delete and existing one, go to Settings - Recruitment - Scorecard Templates :
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You can then use your Scorecard template when setting up a job at the Scorecard stage of the process. Click Import Scorecard to select which template you would like to use.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note : you cannot update the Scorecard used for a job once a candidate in the process has had it filled out.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Completing a Scorecard as an interviewer
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Interviewers will receive an email reminding them to complete a Scorecard shortly before the interview. The Scorecard asks them to rate the candidate from 1 to 5 on each competency and gives the opportunity to leave any notes on the candidate.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When the interviewer saves their Scorecard, their rankings will combine with any other Scorecards provided over the course of the interviews the candidate has had for that job, and will be averaged giving an overall Scorecard score. You can view their Scorecards in the Scorecards tab on the right-hand side of their profile .
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: It is also visible from the job kanban, next to the candidate's name:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: only one Scorecard can be completed per interviewer for a candidate. Interviewers can update their existing Scorecards by going into the candidate's Profile - Scorecards - Edit .
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Scorecard comparison
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Once you have scorecards against numerous candidates in one kanban column, you can choose to compare their scorecards against eachother. To do this, select the candidates you want to compare using the select buttons on the left of their candidate card, then select Other – Compare scorecards from the bar at the bottom.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: This will give you a view of all of the Scorecards left for those candidates, allowing you to get a view of where their strengths are, and see where there are notes that have been added by interviewers.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Should you wish to see more detail, you can select a specific candidate to see all of their scorecards side-by-side. Simply select either their name or the link to the notes and you will see a view similar to this:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Generate your job description with AI
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Writing a job advert can be time consuming. To support businesses who don’t have a job advert prepared for their job, Recruitment has an in-built advert generator using ChatGPT to help create a basic advert that can then be customised by the client.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You can find the Description field under the Job Details part of your set up process.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When you click Generate with AI , you can select the tone of voice you like to use - friendly, fun or professional. Recruitment will then use ChatGPT to create a simple template for your required job.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Candidate Match Scoring
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Understanding how Recruitment helps you see the best candidate matches for your role
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: Recruitment Match Scoring is currently only available in English
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: How is a ‘candidate match score’ calculated?
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When a candidate applies for a role, we use AI to evaluate their CV against the job description, to help you make a better decision of who to focus on.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: This score is based on an algorithm that considers multiple factors, such as job title and skills as taken from the CV, which is then scored against the requirements in the job advert. You can hover over the score to see whether the candidate is a good match for job title and/or key skills in their job advert.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: What does the ‘candidate match score threshold’ mean when I’m creating a new job?
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When setting up a job, you can determine the % match you deem a good threshold to be a match with your job. This will enable you to pull candidates from your candidate database who are above that threshold into the ‘sourced’ column, giving you a way to regenerate your database and have warmer candidates to reach out to.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: The sourced candidates from the database will only be added to your pipeline for a job on your request, so you don’t need to worry about this feature if you only want to invite new applicants to apply for the job, rather than to see if there are any matching candidates in your database already. You can set that % on job setup, but nothing further will happen unless action is taken from the job kanban.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Why does a candidate have a score out of 5 on the kanban rather than candidate match score?
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Scorecards , which are filled in by interviewers once they have interviewed a candidate, will take precedence over the candidate match score, although the candidates match score will still appear on the candidate profile underneath the candidate name, should you wish to review it at a later date.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Customising your hiring process
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: We understand that each business will have their preferred process to running their interviews – perhaps even a different process for each job or department. That’s why our Interview Stages stage is so customisable to your needs.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When you come to the Interview Stage section of job creation, you will set up your screening and interview stages, and decide how many stages you'd like for each. You'll start off with the default of one stage for screening and one for interviewing and can simply tap 'Add new stage' to add more in either section.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You'll also see the option to specify the type of interview you wish to carry out. We offer 5 main types if interview through Recruitment :
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: A phone call A video Q&A - ask the candidate a series of questions in text format, and they will then record their answers to on a video which will then be returned to their candidate profile on Recruitment Video – live 2-way video interview. Choose between Zoom, Google Meets and Microsoft Teams. You'll be able to set this up under My Integrations in the Settings menu. In-person interview Technical test - Choose a test from a list we provide via IKM – our technical testing partner or add your own. We will share the candidates score and breakdown with you once the test is complete.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When you move to the Interview Details section, this is where you can review the email that will be sent to candidates who make it to this stage, set up the duration of your screening or interview, add in any team members who will serve as the panel for the interviews, and you can also switch on automation to allow the system to send an email link for this interview stage as soon as they are moved to this stage, so that you don't have to manually do this for every candidate who is moving through the process.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: This feature is unavailable if you are using blind hiring.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Manually adding a candidate
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Whilst the majority of your candidates will probably come through to Recruitment as applications, where candidates use their CV to parse and pre-fill their details into the application form which is then submitted directly into Recruitment , you may have the odd few candidates that you with to manually added to your database. Candidates can either be added to a job but selecting the “+” in the top right corner and selecting Add candidate :
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Or by using the Candidates section from the navigation bar and selecting the Import Candidates button
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You can either add candidates individually, or in bulk using a .zip file.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: If you wish to add a CV to a candidate profile, If you head to your candidate database on Recruitment , and tap on any candidate that does not currently have a CV on their profile,  select on 'CV Actions' and 'Add CV' when viewing their profile and you will be able to add the CV.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Collecting a portfolio from candidates
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You may require candidates to provide a portfolio as part of your application process. Candidates will be able to provide a link to their portfolio on your job's Apply page:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: This field is optional, so we recommend stating that this is a requirement in the job description.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You are also able to add files to an existing candidate's profile by heading to their profile and selecting Edit then adding the link in at Portfolio Url
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Adding notes and giving feedback on candidate profiles
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: The easiest way to give a quick indication of your thoughts on a candidate profile is the use the “thumbs up” or “thumbs down” towards the middle top of the candidate profile. This is tracked in the notes section below against whoever carries out the action.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: The notes section on a candidate's profile can be used to store any thoughts, updates or information about the candidate. You can add notes to a candidate by using the text box on the right hand side of their profile. Once a note is saved, this will be stored under the candidate's Notes tab. If a note is made Private , only the person who created it, all Admins and the Job Owner will be able to view it. If the candidate's profile had been opened from within a job kanban, then the title of that job will also appear alongside the note, like this:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Hiring in multiple locations
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: As more and more businesses transition to remote working, with some doing this on a global level, you may find you are recruiting for a role that does not require a specific location or you might be recruiting for a role that you need to locate in multiple offices/locations.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: We would recommend creating your job description for this role, and then duplicating it, so you have a job created for each individual location (of course you can then go in and edit each job to ensure its accurate for the location). We'd also recommend including the location in the job title - this way, as applicants are moving through the process, you'll know which location they are applying for.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: To duplicate a job, simply head to your Jobs tab, and tap on the three dots at the end of the row for the relevant job and select ' Duplicate '. You can then tap into the duplicate job and make any necessary changes with ease.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Using email templates
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Recruitment has built in a series of email templates for you to use throughout your recruitment process without you having to start from scratch. Of course, you may prefer to make them feel more on-brand or adapt to your tone of voice – that’s absolutely possible! You are also able to create custom templates to use alongside the system templates which you might want to use for additional purposes.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Available email templates
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You can find email templates by heading to Settings - Recruitment - Email Templates . You'll find a list of system templates which we have created for you to use. The intention of these templates is to serve a purpose in your recruitment process – for example, enabling a candidate to schedule an interview or answer some screening questions. As such, please ensure that you leave all of the tags in place so that the original purpose of the email can be maintained, but feel free to edit the wording around that to feel more fitting to your company.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Create custom email templates
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: If you'd like to create your own templates, simply tap on 'Custom' and 'Add Template' and you'll then have the opportunity to fill in the purpose of the template, the subject , and then the email body .
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You can also set the visibility of the template:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Tick 'Make this Private' when you want to be the only one to use the template Untick 'Make this Private' when you need everyone in the hiring team to be able to view and use the custom template
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Once you're happy with how it looks, just tap 'Save' and the template will be stored under your custom templates, and available for your colleagues if you have set to being publicly available. You can then select templates to email candidates throughout the hiring process at your leisure.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Organising interviews
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Recruitment has the complexity to handle 1-1 interviews, where the candidate and interviewer are the only attendees, panel style where multiple interviewers take part at the same time, and sequential interviews where there are multiple parts to the same interview stage. To set this up at job creation, navigate to the Interview Details section and select the “+” button with Edit details next to it on the section of the Interview process that you wish to amend. This will open a box with additional information so that you can add the required details for your preferred interview type, for example the preferred video interview type (Zoom, Teams or Meet) or the address for an in-person interview. You can then also add the name of the person/people you wish to attend on the client side and determine the duration of the interview.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Should you wish to add multiple attendees, simple type in the Members box and select which team members you wish to attend. If a team member isn’t offered, they probably haven’t been given access to Recruitment , so you might need to speak to your administrator to ensure they are available to add moving forwards.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: From here, you can also review the email template that Recruitment will automatically send to candidates for this interview stage and can choose whether you want automation off or on. Our default setting is that automation is OFF, so don’t worry if that’s not for you! If you toggle automation on, the green robot will be highlighted, and any candidates dragged and dropped into this stage will automatically be sent the invite to self-schedule.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: using automation does require the relevant interviewers to have synced Cronofy in My Integrations in settings and to have entered their days and hours of work in My Preferences . If we don’t have those details, you automation will fail and you will be informed, for example, that a certain user hasn’t synced their calendar.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Using sequential interviewing is also extremely easy and saves considerable time by removing the back and forth looking to calendars and syncing with both interviewers and candidates. When you are setting up the interview details on job creation, select the Add Interview button to add a second (or more!) part to the stage of the interview process you wish to add the additional interview to.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When selecting the time slot, the candidate will see that it is multi-part and will be able to select a time that works for them.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: Interviews with multiple parts must use the same type of interview for each part within a stage.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Syncing a Hired Candidate in Recruitment (through HRM integrations)
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Once you've hired your candidate through Recruitment , you can sync their details to create your newest team member in your HRM . Here's how.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When you move your candidate to the 'Hired' stage, you have the option to sync this candidate's information to create your newest team member in Recruitment . You can either do this immediately or wait and complete this later.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: Most HRM determine that you have created a new employee once you have synced the new candidate across, meaning you will start paying for their access. It’s important that this is clear to users and that this only happens once to avoid having duplicate employees in the HRM.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Syncing a candidate when moving them to 'hired'
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When you move the candidate across to the Hired column in your kanban board, you will get a pop up asking if you would like to ‘Sync now’ or sync later. blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: You can only sync a candidate once to Recruitment to make sure you're ready!
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: When you are ready to sync, find the job in the job kanban and click on the candidate you wish to sync with the HRM. On the candidate's profile, click 'Sync now' which will create the team member in your HRM for you, ready to invite them to onboard!
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: You can only sync a candidate once to Recruitment to make sure you're ready!
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: You'll then be given the option to close job which archives this job, or continue hiring if you are planning on hiring more than one candidate for the role.

blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Job title

blocks.text: Start date

blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Add a new recruitment agency
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: To set up a new recruitment agency, navigate to Settings – Company – Agencies – Add new agency. There you can fill in information such as agency name, rate you work with them at and upload any terms that have been agreed. You also have a box to write any notes, for example the roles that you might use them for.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job
Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Once you ‘save’ you’ll have the option to add them to an existing role. Simply select the job your wish to share with the recruiter from the drop down.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Then you can add the individual recruiter from the agency that you want to add to Recruitment . To do this, type the email address of the user and press enter or select the ‘Add’ button.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Note: Only Account Owners and Account Admins can add and manage agencies
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Manage users in an existing agency
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Head to Settings - Company – Agencies . If you click on the name of the agency, you will be able to see which users have been added. It will show you which have successfully completed onboarding, which which have been invited but not yet accepted. Should you wish to resend the invite, that is possible. Please ensure the user checks their junk if they don’t receive the invite.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

blocks.text: Clicking on the number of candidates they have submitted will bring up the profiles of these candidates, so you are able to track their effectiveness. This also tracks through to your source reporting, ensuring you get a good view as to which agencies are performing for your company.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Setting up a job

Integrating job boards with Recruitment
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Integrating job boards

blocks.text: At the final stage of creating a job – Sharing – you can also choose to publish the job on a number of job boards.  Currently, you can automatically post your advert to any of the free job sites we are directly integrated with - Adzuna, Jooble, CareerJet and Google Jobs.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Integrating job boards

blocks.text: Simply toggle on any of the free job boards where you would like your advert to appear:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Integrating job boards

blocks.text: The advert will then automatically pushed through XML feed to be posted on the job site, and your applicants will appear under Applied in your job kanban, tracked through to the job board where they arrived. # Simployer One - Recruitment - Linkedin

How to post your jobs to LinkedIn with Simployer Recruitment

There are three ways you can share your job to LinkedIn through Recruitment: LinkedIn company feed post, basic adverts (which are free) or paid adverts.

Note: Depending on your LinkedIn plan, there may be costs associated with adding jobs to your company page - this is something you will be able to handle and manage with LinkedIn and not with Recruitment .

LinkedIn free job posting

To connect your company LinkedIn page, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations .

Select LinkedIn Jobs Basic in the pop up, and input your Company ID. Your LinkedIn Company ID is a string of numbers, usually 6 to 9 digits long, that is unique to your company. The guide here explains where to find this code.

You will then be able to post your jobs to LinkedIn from the Sharing stage of job set up - simply toggle on InJobs under Free Job Boards .

LinkedIn paid job posting

To connect your company LinkedIn page, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations .

Select LinkedIn Jobs Premium in the pop up, and input your Company ID. Your LinkedIn Company ID is a string of numbers, usually 6 to 9 digits long, that is unique to your company.

Once your Company ID is entered, click connect an account to authenticate your account and verify your Contract ID (this field will auto-populate).

You will then be able to post your jobs to LinkedIn from the Sharing stage of job set up - simply toggle on InJobs under Paid Job Boards .

Sharing to your LinkedIn company feed

If you're the Recruitment Account Owner or an Admin on Recruitment , you can set up a company-level integration with LinkedIn which will enable you to post jobs from your company as a feed post.

Note: The person enabling this integration must have admin access for their company LinkedIn account for jobs to post to these pages and set up this integration. If they are an admin for multiple companies, then the job will post from all companies they are an admin for so we recommend checking this before you go ahead.

To set up this integration, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations . Next to LinkedIn, there is the option to “Connect”.  You'll then be prompted to sign into your LinkedIn account and Save .

You will then be able to toggle LinkedIn on and off at the Sharing stage of job.

Note: This LinkedIn integration will not post the job onto the company page. If you wish to post a basic job to your company page, please use the LinkedIn free job postings or Premium job postings.

# Simployer One - Recruitment - Simployer Recruitment apps for Microsoft Teams and email access

Modified on Fri, 13 Mar at 8:35 AM

Approving Recruitment apps for Microsoft Teams and email access

If your organisation’s security settings require you to have an administrator approve access via Microsoft, you may receive an error message when trying to connect via Microsoft, Cronofy (gaining Calendar availability) or Teams.

What information do we require

In order to make the most of some of Recruitment's automation, we need consent to:

Send and receive emails from a user's email account triggered on Recruitment (via the Recruitment App for Email) Help schedule interviews with access to a user's Team calendar to find available interview slots and schedule meetings (via the Recruitment App for Teams)

This will only apply to users in an organisation who have access to the reseller’s HR system, a Recruitment account, and have set up these integrations through their Recruitment settings.

How to approve

Go to Enterprise Applications

Under Security , click on Consent & Permissions In the User Consent Settings section:

Ensure Allow user consent for apps is selected

In the Admin Consent Settings section:

Set 'Users can request admin consent to apps they are unable to consent to' to YES

Under 'Who can review admin consent requests' , add the users who can review the app Click Save

Go to All Applications under 'Manage'

Select the App ( Simployer Recruitment App for Teams or Simployer Recruitment App for Email - this process will need to be completed for both) Go to Properties Click the Delete button at the top to remove the application

Try to connect again on Recruitment and send the consent request for the App

Return to Enterprise Applications

Click on Admin consent requests under Activity and approve the app

Reconnect the app and you should be good to go!

Note: If you have already approved these applications and are still unable to connect, please ask your administrator to revoke consent for both applications and follow this set up guide when re-approving the request to ensure connectivity.

blocks.text: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed
How to post jobs to Indeed with Recruitment (Indeed sponsored jobs)
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: Learn how to post your jobs into Indeed and make them available to candidates
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: Note : After you share your job to your company's Indeed account, you need to sponsor them in order to make them available to candidates. You can read more about sponsored jobs in Indeed on their website .
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: Connect Simployer Recruitment to Indeed
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: To connect your company's Indeed page to your Recruitment account, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations and toggle Indeed on.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: Type in your company name exactly as it appears in Indeed.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: Note: company names are case-sensitive in Indeed.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: If you already have an Indeed Campaign, type it here. Otherwise leave it blank and you can always define it later through Indeed.
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: Post a job to Indeed
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: Once you have connected Indeed to your Recruitment account, you will be able to post your jobs to Indeed from the Sharing stage of job set up. Simply toggle on Indeed under Paid Job Boards .

blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

blocks.text: I can not see my job in Indeed, what should I do?

Make sure you create a campaign for the transferred jobs.

content.text:
# Simployer One - Recruitment - Creating your career page

Creating your career page

Create and customise your careers page

Recruitment enables you  to create and customise your own careers site in just a few clicks so that you can easily share your job openings, showcase your employer brand and get candidates excited about what your company offers. As an Account Owner or Admin, you can view and edit your careers site by heading to Settings - Career Site - Customise to get started.

When creating and customising your careers site you are able to:

Add your company logo Replace imagery Update your text Add, remove and reorder sections Customise your fonts and colours Add company navigation links

To add your company's logo at the top of your careers page, head to Edit - Upload your new image - Open.

Replacing images

To change the images in your careers page, Edit - Upload your new image - Open.

From here you'll be asked to crop your images to be optimised for both desktop and mobile. You can zoom in and out to get the fit you are looking for.

Note: your images must be less than 5MB.

Updating text

When you begin with customising your careers site, you'll find we've left some placeholder text and best practices you might want to follow, including the Page Title and 'About Us' section. All of these are editable on page, making it simple to adapt to your company messaging.

Adding, removing, and reordering sections

You can add more sections from our templates by heading to Settings - Add a section - Hover over the section and click Add. The newly added section will default to the bottom of the page, but can be adjusted to your desired location.

If you want to change the order of these sections, you can do this by Settings - Reorder page . You can drag and drop to reorder, and use the “trash” icon to remove a section you no longer need.

Changing your fonts and colours

You can update the font, colours, and button styles to match your company's brand and style by heading to Settings - Style .

Updating your navigation links

You can add or edit your company's social media pages (LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram and more). These can be added under Settings - Navigation Links.

You can also add any additional links you would like in either the header or footer of your career page.

Preview and publish your careers site

When you've added the content of your career page, you can preview it before publishing. To do this, head to Settings in your careers page editor, then Preview .

This will open in a new tab for you to review.

Publishing your careers site

Once you're happy with your preview, you can publish your careers page. To do this, head to Settings in your careers page editor, then Publish . Until you choose to publish the page, it’s not publicly available.

Your career page's URL can be found in Settings - Career Site - Settings - Link to careers page . You can copy this URL to use on your website as a redirect from your “Careers” or “Jobs” page

Integrating with your existing career page

We also offer an API and iFrame giving you flexibility in how you display your live jobs, if you wish to integrate into an existing careers page.

Note: you may need support from an IT contact within your organisation to get this integration up and running.

iFrame integration

The easiest way to integrate is by using the iFrame. Your iFrame code can be found under Settings - Career Site - Settings . This can then be copied, and embedded into your website code base where you would like your vacancies to appear.

This will bring up a box that looks similar to the “jobs” section of the career builder on Candidly, where vacancies you post on Recruitment will be displayed if you select 'Make your job visible' at the Sharing stage of job set up. When a prospective applicant clicks on one of the vacancies, they'll be taken through to the apply page that we host on Recruitment for that job, enabling the candidate to submit their application with ease directly into your kanban for your review.

The text colour used here can be edited at Settings - Company - Profile - Brand Colour

API integration

You can also integrate Recruitment with your career page using our API, which allows for greater customisation of how the jobs appear on your site.

The API key and documentation can be found under Settings - Integrations - Jobs API .

blocks.text: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles
User Roles
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: There are four main permission levels in Recruitment - Account Owner, Admin, User and Reviewer. Account Owners can:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: Add and remove other users and determine permission levels (please check the specifics of the integration with the HRIS partner which may impact where user provisioning is selected) Complete the key setup tasks for their account, such as creating the privacy Policy and setting up a career page Access all other product features at Admin-level
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: Admins can:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: Manage all jobs & candidates Customise their careers page View all reports (account-wide) Adjust and manage default templates and create custom templates Manage team and overall agency permissions, as well as company-level integrations
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: Users can:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: Manage jobs they created, including candidates that were involved in them Enable personal profile integrations, but not company level ones View templates and create/edit custom templates Access all other product features at Reviewer-level
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: Reviewers can:
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: View jobs that have been assigned to them – they can’t create a job Participate in interviews Fill in scorecards for candidates in jobs they are part of the hiring team for Receive relevant notifications in the Communication Centre (same as all permission levels)
blocks.section: Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

blocks.text: Note: the best way to view this is that admins have full visibility of everything across all users, users have full visibility for all jobs they are involved in, and reviewer level have the lowest permission, only being able to respond to actions required within the jobs they are added to the hiring team for – eg. completing a scorecard or leaving a note against a candidate
